note:
**Coverage.** Twenty-nine pages, thirty-one measured regions on eighteen of them, all
accounted once: ten figure rows, eight table rows and thirteen excluded regions. Six
printed tables produce eight table rows because Tables 5 and 6 are each one caption over
two separately boxed grids, and no printed exhibit anywhere in the paper owns zero
regions - the miscount here runs the other way from place to table, not from table to
place.

**This is a resale scan and the scan talks back.** A Chinese shop line
("精品数模资料，...淘宝店铺：闵大荒工科男的杂货铺！") prints above nine of the
region-bearing pages and the caption detector reads it as `caption_above` there, four
times over a raster and five times over a code frame. It is
never a caption: it is a watermark, it repeats verbatim on every page, and every figure
in the paper keeps its real caption on the artifact's other side. Text-layer work on this
paper has to ignore that string, and any census that trusts `caption_above` here will
record nine captions that do not exist.

**Boundary between exhibit and equation is the hardest call in this paper.** The figures
are pasted rasters, but the MATHS is pasted too: p10's whole optimisation model, p13's
suburban model and the `s.t.` spill that opens p13 are all equation blocks rendered as
images, and p15's three logistic regressions and p18's Minkowski distance arrive as
display bands that the detector boxes because they are the widest thing on the page.
Four of the thirteen exclusions are equation images and three are equation bands. The
rule that separates them from a figure: a caption on the page, or a raster with axis
furniture, or a grid with rules. Nothing else in this paper is an exhibit.

**Caption side is the cleanest signal in the paper.** All ten figures below, all eight
table rows above, no exception - not even the two figures that sit at the very top of
their page (Figure 8 opens p17, Figure 10 opens p19) where the text layer's order makes
the caption look as though it precedes the art. The captions there are still physically
under the box; only the box's position in the margin is unusual.

**Table custody splits two ways.** Table 1 is a normal caption-over-grid with the caption
OUTSIDE the measured box, which is why the caption detector dropped it. Tables 5 and 6
are one caption over two grids each - a goodness-of-fit block and a maximum-likelihood
block, boxed separately, 30 pt apart - so the join between region and exhibit has to be
made grid by grid here too, the same rule a sibling paper in this run (P-C-2018-82150)
needed for a fused appendix box.

**Headerless grids are the norm, not the exception.** Six of the eight table rows print
no header row: Table 2's stub column says Degree and Year, Table 3's says Index and
Country, Table 4's says NAV, NCS, AST and NSC, and each first data row does the header's
work. The contract demands a header count of at least one, so those rows record one and
say so; only the appendix grids have a real two-row header, a merged title over a column
band.

**The appendix is code, not figures.** Pages 24-29 return zero image XObjects and no
fill-image operator. Page 24 holds the only printed grids; pages 25-29 hold a two-column
MATLAB listing and a SAS run, framed by a stroked rectangle on p25 and by filled hairline
polygons on p26-29, all six excluded `not-an-exhibit`. The SAS block on p29 is the program
that generated Tables 5 and 6, so the appendix is self-contained: results, then the code
that made them.

**Apparatus limits worth keeping.** Boxes truncate at the image rect for rasters and at
the rule for grids, so a figure box misses its tick labels and a table box misses its
caption - the caption side has to be read from the ink, never from the bbox edge. On p8
and p11 the box's lower edge crosses the caption's line box by 1.5 and 0.5 pt while the
glyph ink stays outside, a graze that would flatter a naive overlap test. Table 1's
numbers are flush left at a single x, and its rural row prints 170450 with the separator
missing while the other rows carry commas, which is the kind of defect that only a crop
shows.

The page returns zero image XObjects and no fill-image operator, so the box is a frame drawn round text, not a pasted screenshot. One 7.8x12 pt pale-yellow highlight box at x91-99, y665-678 is the only fill in it. Heading 'Logistic model' prints at y591 above the frame. Not an exhibit: it is the program that generated the two appendix tables, and it is the second code frame the page carries.
rules: Ten numbered figures and six numbered tables fill thirty-one measured regions across eighteen of twenty-nine pages: ten figure rows, eight table rows and thirteen exclusions, every region accounted exactly once [place.doc_order].

Placement follows the section's job, not the exhibit's type: the two population maps open their divisions (3.1, 4.1), the model sections 4.2 and 4.3 get equations and no artwork at all, the answers section 4.5 collects six of the ten figures, and the appendix holds only grids [place.section_path].

Exhibits cluster by section kind - other 6, model 5, appendix 4, introduction 2, sensitivity 1 - and not one lands in a kind called 'result', because this paper never labels an answer section a result section [place.section_kind].

All eighteen rows sit inside the body of the page and none takes a page to itself: seven fall in the top third, five in the middle and six at the foot, and the largest artwork covers 9.6 per cent of its page [place.page_zone].

Caption side is a property of the TYPE and admits no exception in this paper: all ten figures print their caption below the artwork and all eight table rows print theirs above the grid [caption.position].
Figures and tables run independent counters with no section prefix - Figure 1 to 10 and Table 1 to 6, always 'Number:' with a colon and always in that capitalisation [caption.numbering].
Every caption is a bare noun phrase: no unit, no variable named, no condition, no conclusion and no verb, so the caption never argues [caption.voice].

Captions stay short - seven of the sixteen printed captions run five words or fewer counting the label itself, and the longest is nine - and length does not track the exhibit's importance: the paper's central map and its sensitivity table both get four words [caption.words].
Not one caption states a unit, though the artwork behind it usually has one: the unit lives in the axis label, in the table cell or in the prose [caption.units].
Only two captions mention a variable at all, both through a symbol-free noun ('lag index', 'market share'), and none states a condition or draws a conclusion [caption.concludes].
The artwork is overwhelmingly cartographic: four map-or-plan-view rasters, four line drawings, one scatter and one orthogonal dendrogram, and no bar chart anywhere in the paper [geometry.family].
Legends are rare and never necessary: eight of the ten figures carry none and the two that do keep the key inside the map area with two or three text entries [geometry.legend].
No artwork in the paper carries a colourbar; the density and convenience maps encode in flat discrete fills and the shading is described by the prose instead [geometry.colorbar].
Nothing is three-dimensional: ten figures, zero perspective bars, zero surfaces, zero isometric axes [geometry.three_d].
Every figure is a single panel - no composite, no side-by-side pair, no shared axis - which is why ten printed figures produce exactly ten boxes [geometry.panel_count].

Where a key would be needed the paper labels the series INLINE instead: F(x) and G(x) on the two lag sketches, Early/Mid-term/Late inside the investment curve, the country index on the dendrogram's leaves [geometry.data_labels].
Printed numbers are almost absent from the artwork: only Figure 9 graduates its axes fully, and no figure prints a value on the data itself [geometry.printed_numbers].
Table size tracks the data and only the appendix grows tall, because the appendix is the only place a table has to reproduce a statistical printout rather than a summary [table.rows].
Column count is fixed at five for a country comparison and six for a parameter sweep, and the two-row timeline is the paper's only ten-column grid [table.cols].

Six of the eight table rows print NO header row at all - the stub column carries the labels and the first data row does the header's work - while the four appendix grids print a merged title row above a column header, two header rows each [table.header_rows].

Rules split by origin of the grid: Table 2, Table 4 and the four appendix grids are completely boxed in 0.48 to 0.72 pt horizontals and verticals, Table 1 alone is rule-only booktabs, and Table 3 is the hybrid - five horizontals with four verticals BETWEEN columns and no outer side rules [table.rule_style].

Row shading appears once and it encodes something: Table 4 fills the two output rows (NCS, NSC) grey and leaves the two input rows white, and Table 2's grey sits on COLUMNS 10, 30, 50 and 90~100 in both rows, breaking at 70 and 80, so it is a malformed column band, not row banding [table.zebra].
Only the appendix merges cells, and it merges the same cell four times: each grid's title row spans the full width and the vertical rules stop beneath it [table.merged_cells].
Not one grid puts a unit in its header or in a line above it - the only unit-bearing cells are Table 2's per-cent degrees, where the sign is part of the stub label [table.units_in_header].

No grid aligns on the decimal point: Table 5's second grid starts -1.2326 and 0.2176 at the same left x, and the NAV sweep's single decimal aligns with the integers only by coincidence [table.decimal_aligned].

Seven of the eight table rows stay inside the measure at 72 to 81 per cent of it, and the one that tries for the full width - Table 2 - reaches 99 per cent, so the overrun pattern of a wide table is replaced here by a boxed grid at the measure's edge [table.width].
No table continues across a page break, including the nine-row appendix grids, while the code listing does run unbroken from p25 to p29 [table.continued].

Citation is almost absent: only two exhibits are ever named in the prose by number - 'as shown in figure 2' and 'From Figure 3' - and both are named on the page that prints them, so the paper introduces by deixis and never by reference [mention.style].

A lead sentence is present for all eighteen rows but it names the subject rather than the artwork: 'The dividing results are as follows.', 'The information is shown as below.', 'The curve is exponential.' [mention.lead_sentence].
Reading sentences are rare - four of eighteen rows quote one - because this team stops at the caption and lets the next paragraph carry the interpretation [mention.trail_sentence].

Three exhibits are introduced before the page that draws them: Figure 8 on p16 and Figure 10 on p18 by one page each, and Tables 5 and 6 on p15 by nine, where the prose says only 'the test results are shown in the appendix' [mention.lead_pages].
Counts are one or two per cited exhibit and never accumulate: no exhibit in the paper is discussed again after the section that introduces it [mention.count].
